result.title: Introduction
result.summary:
REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP)
Retirement Plan and Related Consulting Services
May 12, 2011
American Academy of Actuaries 1850 M Street, NW Suite 300 Washington, DC 20036 ATTN: Steve Knell Tel (202) 785-6933 Fax (202) 872-1948 knell@actuary.org
Introduction
The American Academy of Actuaries (Academy) periodically conducts both formal and informal reviews of its service provider contracts. These due diligence processes are designed to assist Academy staff in evaluating comparative levels of vendor service, capabilities, and pricing. The Academy is currently conducting such a review related to the administration of its retirement plans and this RFP is part of that process.

result.title: Background
result.summary: The Academy serves the public and U.S. actuarial profession through independent policy analysis, professional standards and education, public-interest work, public awareness, member development, coordination among U.S. actuarial associations, and global representation. It is a 501(c)(6) nonprofit with a $11 million budget, 17,200 members, 43 staff, revenue primarily from dues, and public affairs, communications, membership, professionalism, and administrative programs; website, audited financial statements, and Form 990 are referenced. It sponsors two defined contribution plans (money purchase and 401(k), both with MassMutual and the same administrator) and a separately administered defined benefit plan, with a possible DC merger. Plan details cover sponsors, administrators, investments, assets, contributions, participation, eligibility, and entry dates. They describe contribution types, loans and investment changes, valuations, vesting, retirement ages and benefits, payout options, in-service or hardship withdrawals, disability and death benefits, and Academy Treasurer trusteeship. Employee contacts include senior executive, finance, and HR staff; a five-member Personnel and Compensation Committee, including pension experts, oversees benefits.

result.title: Scope of Work
result.summary: The Academy seeks proposals to provide comprehensive services for its three employee retirement plans, including plan design, installation, consolidation, termination, amendments, IRS qualification and tax filings, compliance, eligibility and contribution/forfeiture calculations, loans, distributions and tax disclosures, vesting, required nondiscrimination and statutory testing, plan documents and participant communications, actuarial valuations, financial reporting, trust accounting, recordkeeping, administration, and investment management. Services also include census and plan specifications, account and benefit statements, participant education, Summary Annual Reports, and PBGC/DOL reporting such as Form 5500. The vendor should understand the Academy and employees’ retirement needs and deliver excellent service and work product. Desired qualities are proactive benefit solutions, collaboration with staff, volunteers, and employees, creative design and administrative ideas, timely responsiveness, ethical and meticulous professionalism, and comprehensive coordination of all requirements, in-house or outsourced, including investment management.

result.title: Proposal Requirements
result.summary: Proposals may be submitted electronically or in hardcopy and must address 23 requirements: firm background, staffing and ERISA counsel, client and plan counts, 2010 client gains/losses, planned conversions, insurance, privacy and security, legal/administrative actions, participant support and enrollment education, statements and quality standards, services and pricing, direct and indirect compensation, plan-document and custodian options, sample agreement, fund offerings and information, plan reports, SAS 70 report status, and five qualifying nonprofit references. Respondents may add a narrative proposing other improvements. Proposal information is confidential; incomplete submissions may be rejected. Proposals are due May 31, 2011, to Steve Knell. Finalist interviews begin the week of June 6; further interviews or on-site due diligence may follow, with selection expected by June 30, 2011.

result.title: Proposal Submission, Confidentiality, and Selection
key_items: Failure to address all of these items may result in the Academy removing your proposal from consideration.
result.summary: Failure to address all requested items may lead to removal from consideration. Respondents are encouraged to suggest additional options or opportunities to strengthen the Academy’s retirement programs. All information shared during the proposal process is confidential. Proposals are due May 31, 2011, and should be sent to Steve Knell using the previously provided contact information. Finalist interviews with Academy staff and volunteers begin the week of June 6; later steps may include Board or Committee interviews and on-site due diligence. The Academy expects to select a proposal by June 30, 2011.
